column2: Back

#separator:: Web-app hacking methodology — the three stages?
column2: Footprint the app → Analyze inputs (params, cookies, headers, APIs) → Attack the surface (auth, session, access control, input validation, logic).

#separator:: Where does SQL injection get covered?
column2: Its own module — Module 15 — though it is still OWASP A03 Injection.
Broken Access Control (includes IDOR); the #1 category.
Injection — SQLi, command injection, and XSS all live here.
Software & Data Integrity Failures — includes insecure deserialization.
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — its own standalone category.
A01 Broken Access Control — an authorization bug, not an input bug.
A03 Injection (XSS was folded into Injection in the 2021 list).
Payload saved server-side (DB/comment); runs for every viewer of the page.
Payload echoed straight back from the request; fires when the victim clicks a crafted link.

#separator:: DOM-based XSS — where does it execute?
column2: Entirely in client-side JS via a sink like innerHTML/eval; the payload never reaches the server.
Context-aware output encoding + CSP (plus HttpOnly/SameSite cookies) — not input filtering alone.

#separator:: CSRF — who is tricked and to do what?
column2: The victim's browser is tricked into submitting an authenticated state-changing request.

#separator:: SSRF — who is tricked and to do what?
column2: The server is tricked into making a request, often to internal services or cloud metadata.
Cloud metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254 to steal instance credentials.
Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.
Egress allow-list, block link-local/internal IPs, and use IMDSv2.
Insecure Direct Object Reference — tamper a predictable id (1001→1002) to reach another user's object.

#separator:: Fix for IDOR / broken access control?
column2: Server-side, per-object authorization checks with deny-by-default.
LFI reads a local file via ../ traversal; RFI pulls a remote file (needs allow_url_include).
../ sequences (e.g. ?page=../../../../etc/passwd) to escape the web root.
Chain with ; or | (e.g. 127.0.0.1; id); fix = avoid the shell / pass args safely, not a blocklist.
Upload an executable script (shell.php) into a web-served dir → web shell → RCE.
Validate type server-side, store off the web root, disable execution in the upload dir, randomize names.

#separator:: What is XXE and what does it enable?
column2: XML External Entity — external entity (file:///etc/passwd) enables file read, SSRF, and DoS; fix = disable DTDs/external entities.
Reconstructing untrusted serialized objects → RCE / logic abuse; OWASP A08.
Session id set before login and not rotated, so a known id is hijacked; fix = regenerate the id on login.
Proxy the browser → capture request → send to Repeater → tamper one parameter at a time → observe the response.
It confirms findings; the intercepting proxy is where you actually understand the vuln.

#separator:: PAM: remove hardcoded DB/API creds from web.config?
column2: Deliver secrets at runtime via CyberArk CCP/Conjur and rotate them with CPM.

#separator:: PAM: why run the web app as a least-privilege service account?
column2: So a web shell or LFI inherits nothing useful — no local admin, no reusable domain creds.

#separator:: PAM: protect a privileged web/admin console session?
column2: CyberArk Secure Web Sessions — record, isolate, and protect the session.
